newsitem.title: USA: Settlement to end some U.S. spinal device suits.
newsitem.headline: Settlement to end some U.S. spinal device suits.

text.p: A proposed $100 million settlement is expected to end all 3,000 to 3,500 lawsuits involving spinal fusion devices made by Cleveland-based AcroMed Corp, but suits involving other makers of similar devices are still pending, an AcroMed lawyer said Monday.
Spinal device suits from across the United States are coordinated in U.S. District Court in Philadelphia.

Chief Judge Emeritus Louis Bechtle last week stayed all proceedings involving AcroMed pending a final settlement agreement, expected in January, the company and a committee of plaintiffs suing it said in a joint statement.
AcroMed lawyer Rick Werder said funds distribution could vary from case to case. The cases are not combined as a class action, but the settlement would be on a class basis, he said.
Under the proposed settlement, AcroMed will establish a fund of $100 million in cash and products liability insurance.

"The settlement is intended to result in the complete release of all products liability claims based on the use of these devices," he said, adding that those who accept it would in essense agree to not file further claims against AcroMed.
The suits contend that devices called pedicle screws, used in spinal fusion surgery to treat a variety of conditions, have led to back pain, nerve damage and other problems.
AcroMed said it believes claims are without merit but settled to end the controversy the suits have caused.

"(The suits) represent a very small fraction of the total number of surgeries" involving AcroMed's devices, which have been in use in the United States since 1983, Werder said. "Most people have been highly satisfied with their surgeries."
An executive of Memphis-based Sofamor Danek Group Inc, another maker of spinal devices involved in separate pending suits, could not be reached Monday for comment.

A Sofamor executive told Reuters Friday he attributed a rise in his company's stock price to news of the AcroMed settlement. Sofamor Danek closed Monday at $32.625, up $1.50 from Friday's close. AcroMed is privately held.
